title: Review this week's token proposals
prompt: Six semantic token names were proposed to Northwind UI this week. The system must support light and dark themes and two brands (Northwind and Tidewater), and follows the grammar `--nw-{category}-{concept}-{property}-{variant}-{state}`. Select every name you would **approve as written**.
hints: For each name, imagine it in dark mode and in the Tidewater brand. Does it still tell the truth?
Watch for color words, theme words, version numbers and names that only fit one component.
explanation: The approved names describe a role: a success border, text on an inverse surface, the focus ring. Each stays accurate in every theme and brand. `orange-badge` describes a look that Tidewater's palette will change, `modal-shadow-v2` encodes history instead of purpose (and the next redesign gives you `v3`), and `dark-surface` breaks in dark mode, where most surfaces are dark. A role-based alternative would be `--nw-color-surface-raised` or `--nw-color-surface-inverse`.

success-border.why: Approve. It names a role (the border of success messages) and follows the grammar's order.

orange-badge.why: Reject. 'Orange' is appearance; when the warning color changes for Tidewater, the name lies.

text-inverse.why: Approve. 'Inverse' means text on the opposite surface, which holds in both themes.

modal-shadow-v2.why: Reject. A version number records history, not purpose, and guarantees a `v3` later.

focus-ring.why: Approve. Every interactive component shares the focus ring, and the role is stable across themes.

dark-surface.why: Reject. In dark mode almost every surface is dark, so the name stops meaning anything.
